md_description: This workflow covers collection of coastal sediment samples across locations and seasons, extraction of microbial DNA, high-throughput 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, and computational processing into an abundance table for community analysis. It links measured microbial composition to environmental context such as coordinates, sediment depth, temperature, salinity, and season to study diversity patterns and ecological associations.

coastal_sediment_sample.reasoning: The coastal_sediment_sample node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic sample identity/origin and the environmental context recorded at collection. I excluded any extraction, library prep, sequencing, file, or computational fields because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any experiment-level identifiers that are typically generated at the root if already present elsewhere, and kept the schema focused on sample provenance and in situ collection context needed to interpret coastal sediment microbial diversity.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the coastal sediment sample, assigned at collection and used to link this entity to downstream extraction and sequencing steps. Format example: CS-001 or siteA_2024-07-15_01.
Human-readable name or code for the coastal sampling location recorded for this sample, such as a beach, estuary, or transect site label.
Geographic latitude of the sampling point in decimal degrees recorded at collection time; typical range -90 to 90. Example: 36.7783.
Geographic longitude of the sampling point in decimal degrees recorded at collection time; typical range -180 to 180. Example: -122.4194.
Depth below the sediment surface from which the sample was collected, measured in centimeters at the time of sampling; typical range 0 to 100 cm depending on study design. Example: 5.0.
Ambient or porewater temperature at the sampling point measured in degrees Celsius during collection; typical coastal sediment range about 0 to 35 °C. Example: 18.6.
Salinity of the sampling environment measured at the collection site in practical salinity units (PSU) or equivalent seawater salinity scale; typical coastal range about 0 to 40 PSU. Example: 31.2.
Season during which the sample was collected, recorded to capture temporal variation in community composition.
Date the sediment sample was collected, recorded in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) to support seasonal and temporal comparisons. Example: 2024-07-15.
Brief description of the sediment sampling method used for this entity, such as grab sample, corer type, or sterile scoop, recorded at collection time to support provenance and comparability.

sediment_dna_extraction.reasoning: The sediment_dna_extraction node is a Process, so I included only process parameters and reagent/workflow details that define how DNA was extracted from the sediment sample, plus a minimal output-quality indicator for extraction success. I excluded sample provenance, capture/instrument settings, downstream library prep, sequencing, file, and derivative fields because those belong to the Entity, Capture, later Process, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided duplicating any sample identifiers or environmental descriptors that are already owned by the coastal_sediment_sample node, and I did not repeat any already_generated process fields from other nodes.

md_schema.descr: DNA extraction protocol or kit used to isolate microbial DNA from the sediment sample at this process step, recorded to support reproducibility. Example: bead-beating plus silica column kit or a named commercial kit.
Bead material used during mechanical lysis, if applicable, for example zirconia/silica or glass beads, recorded as part of the extraction workflow.
Diameter of the lysis beads used during mechanical disruption of sediment cells, measured in millimeters; typical values are about 0.1 to 2.0 mm depending on kit/protocol. Example: 0.5.
Duration of the mechanical/chemical lysis step used during DNA extraction, measured in minutes from start to end of the lysis phase. Typical range is about 1 to 30 minutes. Example: 10.
Temperature at which the lysis/extraction step was performed, measured in degrees Celsius at the process stage; typical range is 4 to 70 °C depending on protocol. Example: 56.0.
Final elution volume used to recover extracted DNA from the purification matrix, measured in microliters at the end of the extraction process. Typical range is about 20 to 200 µL. Example: 50.

Total amount of DNA recovered from the sediment extraction measured after purification and before downstream amplification, reported in nanograms. Typical values vary widely by sediment type and biomass. Example: 12.4.
Concentration of the extracted DNA solution measured after purification and before amplicon library preparation, reported in nanograms per microliter. Example: 6.2.
Indicates whether the extraction blank or negative control showed no detectable contamination at this process step, used as a quality check for the DNA extraction workflow.
Spectrophotometric 260/280 absorbance ratio of the extracted DNA measured after purification and before library preparation; typical clean DNA values are about 1.7 to 2.0. Example: 1.82.

extracted_sediment_dna.reasoning: The extracted_sediment_dna node is an Entity, so I included intrinsic properties of the DNA extract itself: identity, provenance link to the source sample, concentration/quantity, purity/integrity, storage, and whether it is suitable for downstream library prep. I excluded extraction protocol details because those belong to the sediment_dna_extraction Process, and I excluded library prep, sequencing, and file properties because those belong to downstream nodes. I also avoided repeating sample-level environmental metadata already owned by coastal_sediment_sample and did not duplicate any already_generated fields with equivalent meaning.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified sediment DNA extract, assigned after extraction and used to track aliquots into library preparation. Format example: DNA-EX-001 or CS-001_A.
Identifier of the coastal sediment sample from which this DNA extract was obtained, linking the extract back to the parent entity. Format example: CS-001.
Measured concentration of the purified DNA extract prior to 16S library preparation, reported in nanograms per microliter. Typical values depend on biomass and extraction method; example: 5.8.
Total mass of DNA recovered in the extract before any dilution or aliquoting, reported in nanograms. Example: 42.0.
Recovered volume of the purified DNA extract available for downstream library preparation, measured in microliters. Example: 50.
Spectrophotometric 260/280 absorbance ratio for the DNA extract, used as a purity indicator before library preparation; clean DNA is often around 1.7 to 2.0. Example: 1.86.
Spectrophotometric 260/230 absorbance ratio for the DNA extract, used as a secondary purity indicator before library preparation; values near 2.0 are often considered good. Example: 2.05.

Qualitative assessment of DNA integrity for library preparation based on gel, fragment analyzer, or similar check performed after extraction. Use to indicate whether the extract is suitable for amplicon library construction.
Temperature at which the DNA extract was stored after purification and before library preparation, measured in degrees Celsius. Typical values are -20 or -80. Example: -80.
Buffer or solution used to store the purified DNA extract prior to amplicon library preparation, such as nuclease-free water or TE buffer.
Whether the extracted DNA passed the minimum quality criteria required to proceed to 16S amplicon library preparation at this workflow step.

amplicon_library_prep.reasoning: The amplicon_library_prep node is a Process, so I included only the parameters that define how the extracted DNA was amplified, indexed, and prepared for sequencing, along with a brief process-level success/quality indicator. I excluded source sample properties, DNA extract intrinsic properties, instrument capture settings, and downstream library/file outputs because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, the extracted DNA Entity, the Capture node, or the sequencing_library Entity. I also avoided any field names or meanings already generated for earlier nodes, keeping the schema centered on PCR and indexing conditions needed to reproduce the library preparation step.

md_schema.descr: 16S rRNA hypervariable region amplified during library preparation, recorded as the primer-targeted region used in this process step. Example: V3-V4 or V4.
Forward PCR primer sequence used to amplify the 16S target region during library preparation, reported in 5' to 3' orientation. Example: ACTCCTACGGGAGGCAGCAG.
Reverse PCR primer sequence used to amplify the 16S target region during library preparation, reported in 5' to 3' orientation. Example: GGACTACHVGGGTWTCTAAT.
Total PCR reaction volume used for amplicon amplification and indexing, measured in microliters at the library prep step. Typical range is about 10 to 100 µL. Example: 25.
Mass of extracted DNA input into the amplicon library preparation reaction, measured in nanograms at setup time. Typical range depends on protocol and biomass; example: 5.0.
Number of PCR cycles used to amplify and index the 16S amplicon library during this process step. Typical range is about 20 to 35 cycles. Example: 25.
DNA polymerase or master mix used for 16S amplification during library preparation, recorded to support reproducibility. Example: high-fidelity hot-start polymerase or a named commercial mix.
Indexing or barcode scheme applied during library preparation to enable multiplex sequencing, such as dual-index or single-index tagging.
Cleanup or size-selection method applied after amplification/indexing to remove primers, dimers, or contaminants before sequencing. Example: magnetic beads or gel extraction.
Total amount of indexed amplicon library recovered after amplification and cleanup, measured in nanograms at the end of the process. Example: 18.7.
Indicates whether the prepared amplicon library met the study's acceptance criteria for sequencing readiness, assessed after amplification and cleanup.

sequencing_library.reasoning: The sequencing_library node is an Entity, so I included intrinsic properties of the indexed library itself: the library identifier, linkage to the source DNA extract, indexing/barcode composition, fragment size, concentration, mass, and whether the library is sequencing-ready. I excluded PCR/cleanup protocol details because those belong to the amplicon_library_prep Process, and I excluded instrument configuration and raw read/file properties because those belong to the hts_16s_capture Capture and raw_fastq_reads Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating upstream sample/DNA metadata and did not reuse fields already generated for other nodes under semantically equivalent names.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the indexed 16S sequencing library, assigned after library preparation and used to track the library into the sequencing run. Format example: LIB-001 or CS-001_L1.
Identifier of the purified DNA extract used to create this sequencing library, linking the library back to the parent extracted DNA entity. Format example: DNA-EX-001.
i5 index or barcode sequence incorporated into the sequencing library for multiplexing, reported in 5' to 3' orientation. Example: ATCACG.
i7 index or barcode sequence incorporated into the sequencing library for multiplexing, reported in 5' to 3' orientation. Example: CGATGT.

Approximate mean fragment size of the indexed 16S amplicon library before sequencing, measured in base pairs after final cleanup. Typical values for 16S amplicons are about 250 to 700 bp depending on target region. Example: 420.
Measured concentration of the sequencing-ready library prior to loading onto the sequencer, reported in nanograms per microliter. Example: 4.6.
Calculated molar concentration of the sequencing library used for pooling or loading, reported in nanomolar. Typical values are protocol dependent. Example: 12.5.
Total mass of the prepared sequencing library available for sequencing, reported in nanograms. Example: 25.0.
Qualitative assessment of whether adapter or primer contamination remained in the final sequencing library after cleanup, evaluated before sequencing.
Indicates whether the indexed 16S library passed final pre-sequencing checks and was approved for loading on the sequencer.

hts_16s_capture.reasoning: The hts_16s_capture node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration: sequencer identity, manufacturer/model/serial, chemistry and flow cell, run settings, loading parameters, and run-level quality indicators. I excluded sample provenance, library intrinsic properties, raw file properties, and downstream computational outputs because those belong to the Entity, Sequencing Library, Signal, or later Process/Derivative nodes. I also avoided duplicating fields already generated for the library or extraction steps, and I kept the schema focused on what the operator actively configured during sequencing.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the 16S capture session, recorded as part of the instrument configuration. Example: Illumina.
Instrument model used to read the 16S amplicon library during this capture session. Example: MiSeq.
Serial number or unique hardware identifier of the sequencing instrument used in this capture session, recorded for traceability. Format example: M01234.
Unique identifier for the sequencing run or capture session, assigned by the instrument or laboratory workflow. Format example: RUN-2024-07-15-01.
Flow cell or cartridge type loaded on the sequencer for this run, recorded as part of the capture configuration. Example: MiSeq v2 or MiSeq v3.
Sequencing chemistry or reagent kit used during the capture session, recorded to describe the active instrument setup. Example: paired-end 2x250 chemistry.
Configured read length per end in base pairs for the sequencing run, measured as the planned output length at capture setup. Typical values for 16S runs are often 150 to 300 bp. Example: 250.
Indicates whether the sequencing run was configured to generate paired-end reads rather than single-end reads.
Concentration of the prepared library loaded onto the sequencer, reported in pM or equivalent loading units at run setup. Example: 8.0.

Instrument run temperature set during the sequencing session, measured in degrees Celsius if explicitly controlled by the platform. Typical platform-dependent range is about 18 to 25 °C. Example: 20.0.
Observed cluster density on the flow cell during or after run initiation, reported in thousands per square millimeter (k/mm^2) when available. Example: 950.0.
Run-level percentage of bases meeting Q30 or better during the capture session, used as a high-level quality indicator for sequencing performance. Example: 82.5.
Outcome status of the sequencing capture session at completion, used to indicate whether the run finished successfully or encountered problems.

raw_fastq_reads.reasoning: I corrected the raw_fastq_reads schema to remove the colliding read_length_bp field, since that field was already generated for an earlier DAG step. I kept the remaining Signal-level fields that describe the FASTQ artifact itself: file identity, format, size, read count, paired-end role, technical quality summaries, checksum, and compression state. I continued to exclude capture settings, sample metadata, and downstream processing details because they belong to other node types.

md_schema.descr: Path or URI to the raw FASTQ file produced by the sequencing run, recorded as the storage location of this signal artifact. Format example: s3://bucket/run1/sampleA_R1.fastq.gz.
Name of the raw FASTQ file generated by the sequencer, typically including sample and read identifiers. Example: sampleA_R1.fastq.gz.
Technical file format of the raw read signal, which should be FASTQ or a compressed FASTQ variant for this workflow.
Size of the raw FASTQ file on disk, measured in bytes at the time of storage or transfer. Example: 1845239000.
Total number of raw sequencing reads contained in the FASTQ file after instrument output and before any filtering or trimming. Example: 2450000.
Read orientation represented by this FASTQ signal when paired-end sequencing was used. Use to distinguish forward and reverse read files.
Average base-call quality score across reads in the FASTQ file, reported as a Phred score summary for the raw signal. Example: 32.4.
Percentage of bases in the raw reads that are G or C, reported as a technical summary statistic of the FASTQ signal. Example: 54.1.
MD5 checksum of the raw FASTQ file used to verify file integrity during storage or transfer. Format example: 9e107d9d372bb6826bd81d3542a419d6.
Indicates whether the raw FASTQ signal is stored compressed or uncompressed at the file level.

read_processing.reasoning: The read_processing node is a Process, so I included only computational processing parameters that describe how raw FASTQ reads were demultiplexed, quality filtered, trimmed, and oriented, plus a concise output-quality indicator for the processed read set. I excluded raw file properties, capture settings, sample provenance, and downstream denoising/ASV inference details because those belong to the Signal, Capture, Entity, or later Process/Derivative nodes. I also avoided the previously generated field name collision by not using read_length_bp again; instead, I used non-overlapping fields focused on trimming and filtering behavior.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to demultiplex, quality filter, and trim the raw FASTQ reads at this process step. Example: QIIME 2.
Version of the software or pipeline used for read processing, recorded to support exact computational reproducibility. Example: 2024.2.
Method used to assign reads to samples during processing, such as barcode matching or instrument-level demultiplexing.
Minimum per-base Phred quality threshold applied during read filtering, measured as a score cutoff used to retain or discard reads or bases. Typical values are around 20 to 30. Example: 20.
Number of bases removed from the left end of reads during trimming to remove primers, barcodes, or low-quality leading bases, measured in base pairs. Example: 17.
Number of bases removed from the right end of reads during trimming to remove low-quality trailing sequence, measured in base pairs. Example: 20.
Maximum expected errors allowed per read during quality filtering, used as a computational cutoff to retain higher-quality reads. Typical values depend on workflow; example: 2.0.
Indicates whether adapter sequence removal was performed during read processing before downstream denoising.
Indicates whether forward and reverse reads were merged during processing to create single contiguous read sequences before downstream analysis.
Number of reads retained after demultiplexing, quality filtering, and trimming, reported at the end of the processing step. Example: 1800000.
Percentage of raw reads retained after processing, calculated from input FASTQ reads to the post-processing read set. Example: 78.3.
Outcome of the read processing step, used to indicate whether demultiplexing, filtering, and trimming completed successfully.

filtered_reads.reasoning: The filtered_reads node is a Signal, so I included only properties of the processed read artifact itself: file location, format, size, retained read counts, read layout, technical quality summaries, and simple provenance from the previous processing step. I excluded the filtering parameters and software details because those belong to the read_processing Process, and I excluded denoising, merging, and ASV inference details because those belong to later Process/Derivative nodes. I also avoided duplicating any previously generated fields and kept the schema centered on what a user needs to identify and assess the retained read set.

md_schema.descr: Path or URI to the quality-controlled read file produced after initial processing, recorded as the storage location of this signal artifact. Format example: s3://bucket/run1/sampleA_filtered.fastq.gz.
Name of the processed read file retained after filtering and trimming, typically including sample and read identifiers. Example: sampleA_filtered.fastq.gz.
Technical file format of the filtered read signal, such as FASTQ or compressed FASTQ.
Size of the filtered read file on disk, measured in bytes at the time of storage or transfer. Example: 1023456789.
Number of sequencing reads retained after demultiplexing, filtering, and trimming, reported for this processed signal. Example: 1750000.
Number of reads removed during initial processing because they failed quality, adapter, or trimming criteria. Example: 500000.
Percentage of raw reads retained in the filtered read set after initial processing, calculated from input reads to retained reads. Example: 78.3.
Average Phred quality score across the retained reads after initial filtering and trimming, reported as a technical summary statistic of this signal. Example: 34.1.
Median observed read length in base pairs across the retained filtered reads, measured after trimming and before denoising. Example: 240.
Checksum used to verify integrity of the filtered read file during storage or transfer. Format example: 9e107d9d372bb6826bd81d3542a419d6.
Identifier of the upstream processing step that generated this filtered read signal, linking the signal back to the read_processing node. Format example: read_processing.

denoise_and_assemble.reasoning: The denoise_and_assemble node is a Process, so I included only the computational workflow settings that describe how filtered reads were denoised, merged, and chimera-checked, plus a process-level summary of outputs and quality. I excluded signal/file properties of the filtered reads, capture settings, sample provenance, and the resulting ASV table properties because those belong to the upstream Signal, Capture, Entity, or downstream Derivative nodes. I also avoided reusing any already-generated field names and kept the schema focused on algorithmic parameters and performance indicators needed to reproduce the ASV inference step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or algorithm used to denoise filtered reads and infer amplicon sequence variants at this process step. Example: DADA2.
Version of the denoising software or pipeline used for ASV inference, recorded to support computational reproducibility. Example: 1.30.
Number of bases removed from the left end of filtered reads before denoising, measured in base pairs. Example: 0 or 20 depending on workflow.
Length at which filtered reads were truncated before denoising, measured in base pairs, used to standardize read quality for ASV inference. Example: 220.
Maximum expected errors allowed per read during denoising, used as a quality cutoff for ASV inference. Example: 2.0.
Method used to identify and remove chimeric sequences during denoising, such as consensus or pooled chimera checking.
Indicates whether forward and reverse reads were merged during the denoising step to build contiguous amplicon sequences.
Minimum required overlap in base pairs for paired-end read merging during denoising, when merging was performed. Example: 20.
Description of the ASV inference strategy used by the denoising workflow, such as exact sequence inference with error modeling.
Number of denoised reads retained after chimera removal and merging, if applicable, at the end of this process step. Example: 1500000.
Number of unique amplicon sequence variants inferred from the filtered reads at the end of the denoising process. Example: 850.
Outcome status of the denoising and chimera-checking step, used to indicate whether ASV inference completed successfully.

asv_table.reasoning: The asv_table node is a Derivative, so I kept only fields describing the computed abundance table itself: identity, source linkage, storage, format, structure, sparsity, abundance metric, and integrity. I removed the colliding asv_count field because that identifier was already generated earlier in the DAG, and I replaced it with non-overlapping table dimensions specific to the derivative output. I excluded upstream sequencing and denoising parameters as well as downstream ecological interpretation fields because those belong to other node types.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed ASV abundance table, assigned after denoising and used to track the derivative across downstream analyses. Format example: ASV-TBL-001.
Identifier of the upstream denoising process that generated this ASV table, linking the derivative back to the denoise_and_assemble node. Format example: denoise_and_assemble.
Path or URI where the ASV abundance table is stored, recorded as the location of this derivative artifact. Format example: s3://bucket/results/asv_table.tsv.
Technical format of the ASV abundance table file, such as TSV, CSV, BIOM, or HDF5 depending on workflow output. Example: biom.
Number of sediment samples represented as columns or rows in the ASV abundance table, measured as a structural property of the derivative output. Example: 48.
Number of unique ASV features represented in the table, measured as the number of feature rows or entries after denoising. Example: 850.
Number of table cells with nonzero ASV abundance values, used as a sparsity summary for the derived feature table. Example: 120000.
Percentage of zero-valued cells in the ASV abundance matrix, computed from the full table structure as a summary of sparsity. Example: 96.5.
Type of abundance values stored in the ASV table, such as raw counts or normalized abundances, describing the computed matrix content. Example: raw_count.
Sum of all abundances across the ASV table, measured from the computed derivative output and used as a summary of sequencing depth retained in the table. Example: 1500000.
Checksum used to verify integrity of the ASV table file during storage or transfer. Format example: 9e107d9d372bb6826bd81d3542a419d6.

community_analysis.reasoning: The community_analysis node is a Process, so I included only analysis workflow parameters, statistical/computational settings, and process-level outputs or quality indicators. I excluded ASV table structural properties and raw sequencing details because those belong to the upstream Derivative and Signal nodes, and I excluded the final ecological interpretation outputs because those belong to the downstream ecological_results Derivative. I also avoided the previously generated asv_count field collision and focused on analysis choices needed to reproduce the community diversity and association computations.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analysis environment used to compute community diversity and environmental associations from the ASV table. Example: phyloseq.
Version of the community analysis software or package used for this process step, recorded for computational reproducibility. Example: 1.46.
Name of the alpha-diversity metric computed from the ASV table during community analysis, if applicable. Example: Shannon, Simpson, or observed richness.
Distance or dissimilarity metric used to compare microbial composition among samples during community analysis, if applicable. Example: Bray-Curtis or UniFrac.
Ordination method used to visualize or summarize multivariate community patterns during analysis, such as PCoA, NMDS, or PCA.
Statistical test or model used to assess associations between community composition and environmental factors, recorded for the analysis step. Example: PERMANOVA or linear mixed model.
Sample grouping variable used to compare community patterns across categories such as location or season during analysis. Example: season or site.
Method used to correct for multiple hypothesis testing in environmental association analyses, if applied. Example: BH or Bonferroni.
Criteria applied before analysis to filter samples or ASVs from the ASV table, such as minimum prevalence or minimum counts. Example: retain ASVs present in at least 5% of samples.
P-value threshold used to declare significant ecological or environmental associations during analysis. Typical values are 0.05 or lower. Example: 0.05.
Number of output summaries, plots, or statistical result objects produced by the community analysis process. Example: 12.
Outcome status of the community analysis process, used to indicate whether the computation completed successfully.

ecological_results.reasoning: The ecological_results node is a Derivative, so I included only properties of the computed scientific outputs: result identity, source linkage, output file/format, summary statistics, effect sizes/significance summaries, and a high-level interpretation status. I excluded community-analysis parameters because those belong to the upstream Process, and I excluded raw/filtered/ASV table structure because those belong to upstream Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided previously generated field names and kept the schema focused on the end products used to report ecological patterns and environmental associations.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived ecological results package, assigned after community analysis and used to track the output object. Format example: ECO-RES-001.
Identifier of the upstream community analysis process that generated these ecological results, linking the derivative back to the community_analysis node. Format example: community_analysis.
Path or URI where the ecological results file or report is stored, recorded as the location of this derivative artifact. Format example: s3://bucket/results/ecological_summary.pdf or .tsv.
Technical format of the ecological results output, such as PDF, TSV, CSV, HTML, or RDS depending on the analysis deliverable. Example: pdf.
Summary of the alpha-diversity outcome produced by the analysis, such as a table or text descriptor of richness/diversity across samples.
Summary of the beta-diversity or community-composition comparison outcome produced by the analysis, describing separation or clustering among groups.

Environmental variable evaluated in association with microbial community variation in the results output, such as site, depth, temperature, salinity, or season. This field may be used in a row-wise results table or summary record.

Estimated magnitude of the association or group difference reported in the ecological results, using the scale produced by the statistical method applied. Example: R2, correlation coefficient, or model estimate.
Name of the metric used to report association magnitude in the ecological results, such as R2, rho, or log2 fold change.
P-value reported for the ecological association or group comparison in the results output. Typical range is 0 to 1. Example: 0.012.
Multiple-testing adjusted p-value or false-discovery-rate value reported for the ecological result, if correction was applied. Example: 0.034.
Indicates whether the reported environmental association or diversity comparison met the study's significance criterion in the final results.
High-level status indicating whether the derived ecological results were successfully interpreted into a reportable outcome.
